rows.medi_said: اليوم أكلت آآآ، رز مع دجاج teriyaki، و خضرة مختلفة.
rows.why: He used the MSA form دجاج; her sheet row is 'chicken | Jaj | جاج' (also 'Jaaje | جاجة'); she let it pass. Best reading: dialect form of a word he knows.
rows.english: Today I ate rice with teriyaki chicken and different vegetables.

rows.medi_said: What is the word for review?
rows.amal_said: As a noun it's مراجعة. So what's-- what is it as a verb? ... صح، براجع.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked for the word; she supplied مراجعة and براجع (sheet: 'review | Muraaja3a | مراجعة', 'i review | Ana baraaje3 | أنا براجع').

rows.medi_said: آآآ، الشمال الـ، روسيا the, the north of Russia. الشمال.
rows.amal_said: بس، بس شمال روسيا.
rows.why: Idafa: the first word never takes el-; he said الشمال الـ روسيا, she recast شمال روسيا (and again at 05:37 after he repeated 'الشمال الـ روس').

rows.medi_said: Okay. الشمال روس بيكون آآآ برد كتير ويكون بيمطر أو بتثلج.
rows.why: Right after her fix he kept el- on the first word of the idafa (and clipped روسيا to روس); she let it pass this time.
rows.english: The north of Russia is very cold and it rains or snows.

rows.medi_said: برد كتير ويكون بيمطر أو بتثلج.
rows.why: Her sheet has 'it's raining | Betma66er | بتمطر' (feminine, الدنيا); he used the masculine بيمطر then got بتثلج right; she did not react. Best reading.

rows.amal_said: تقدر تحط الدنيا قبل ... الدنيا مطر وثلج، و... مغيمة وعتمة.
rows.why: مغني (singer) is a non-word for 'cloudy'; her sheet: 'it's cloudy | M8ayyme | مغيمة'. She recast the whole weather line with مغيمة; he may have half-fixed it himself ('نوع مغيمة'), so medium.

rows.medi_said: How do I say dark again؟
rows.amal_said: عتمة.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked, she supplied عتمة (sheet: 'darkness | 3etme | عتمة').

rows.medi_said: Is it Asafa؟ Is that, is that stars؟
rows.amal_said: No. ... Storm.
rows.why: He offered عاصفة for 'stars'; she said no, it means storm (sheet: 'storm | 3aasefe | عاصفة', 'star | Nejme | نجمة'), then led him to نجوم.

rows.medi_said: is it أنجم؟ I don't know. أنجم، نجوم،
rows.amal_said: نجوم.
rows.why: She asked 'What's multiple?'; he first repeated نجمة, then invented the plural أنجم before reaching نجوم, which she confirmed. Invented plural pattern = tier 2.

rows.medi_said: الـ المدينة حوالين or الـ المدينة سان فرانسيسكو Oakland
rows.why: English 'or' dropped inside an Arabic sentence; sheet row 'or | Aw | أو'.
rows.english: the cities around, or the cities San Francisco / Oakland

rows.medi_said: الـ المدينة حوالين or الـ المدينة سان فرانسيسكو Oakland ... قريب، قريبًا مني
rows.why: He named two cities with the singular المدينة; she treated the subject as plural (asked for the plural of قريب) but did not fix the noun. Best reading.
rows.english: the cities around, San Francisco and Oakland, are close to me

rows.amal_said: What's the، what's-- وشو جمع غريب؟ ... غراب.
rows.why: Plural subject (the cities) needs the plural adjective قراب; she prompted 'شو جمع قريب؟' and he produced قراب مني (transcript writes her ق as غ).

rows.amal_said: The end. ... مم، آخر الكلمة.
rows.why: Asked how to say 'the end of the word' he said تحت (under); she prompted 'The end', he fixed to آخر الكلمة, she confirmed (sheet: 'last / the end of | 2aa5er | آخر').
Describing the derivation ('then we add a b-') he said مزيد, a noun/MSA form, for the verb بنزيد she had just used (12:02 'قبل ما نزيد'); she answered 'مم'. Best reading.

rows.amal_said: لا، أول الكلمة.
rows.why: He started with el- on the first word of the idafa (الأول الكلمة; he repeats 'الأول الـ' at 12:50); she said لا، أول الكلمة.

rows.medi_said: means to make something stop working.
rows.amal_said: مم. It's not بخرب yet. It's بخرب.
rows.why: He glossed the derived بخرَب as causative 'make something stop working'; she said it is not بخرِّب yet, it is بخرَب (I stop working / break down).

rows.amal_said: mm-hmm. خربت.
rows.why: Past tense she-ending is -at (خربت); he said خربات and asked again at 16:18 ('It's خربات or خربات؟'), she repeated خربت. خربوا.

rows.medi_said: with AC, can I say that? Air conditioning. تباي.
rows.amal_said: مم. تبعيت. We don't-- We haven't discussed تبعيت a lot yet. So تبعيت.
rows.why: He tried the 'mine / belonging to' particle (تبعي) as تباي; she recast the form as تبعيت and said they had not covered it much. Transcript of her form is uncertain.
rows.english: my (air conditioning) / the one that is mine

rows.amal_said: صلحته.
rows.why: For 'I fixed it' he used صحّح (to correct); she recast صلّحته (to repair), a different lexical item.

rows.amal_said: بس still هذا الفعل الثاني. ... أمم، not بخرب. بخرب that would be.
rows.why: In 'everything my fiancee uses breaks' he used the doubled-middle causative (her 'the second verb'); she said not بخرِّب, and at 21:53 gave كل إشي بتستعمله بيخرب. His Arabic is untranscribed.
rows.english: everything my fiancee uses breaks / stops working

rows.medi_said: Uh, but [speaking Arabic] oh, that's right, it's she and not you. [speaking Arabic]
rows.amal_said: بتستعمل.
rows.why: She recast the verb as بتستعمل twice (20:58, 21:13) and he realised 'it's she and not you' - he had conjugated 'uses' for the wrong person. His form is untranscribed.

rows.medi_said: [speaking Arabic] oh, that's right, it's she and not you. [speaking Arabic]
rows.amal_said: بتستعمله.
rows.why: Object fronted (كل إشي) so the verb needs the pointer ending -e: she recast بتستعمله and later spelled out كل إشي بتستعمله بيخرب.

rows.amal_said: بس. بيخرب. بس بيخرب. ... No, because it breaks. يعني خلاص it's kind of another sentence within the sentence.
rows.why: He asked 'do I need to do it for this verb too?' and added the pointer ending to بيخرب; she said no, just بيخرب - 'it breaks' is its own clause.

rows.medi_said: ما، ما تفتحي. ما بهتي، ما بهتي. بي-- بتفتحي
rows.amal_said: With B. ... ما بتحطي...
rows.why: 'If you don't put it in the fridge': he used فتح (open) for حط (put); she recast ما بتحطي (sheet: 'put | 7ott | حط', 'i put | Ana ba7ut | أنا بحط').
rows.english: if you don't put (it in the fridge)

rows.amal_said: With B. ... ما بتحطي...
rows.why: In the iza-clause 'إذا ما ... ' he dropped the b- (ما تفتحي); she said 'With B' and gave ما بتحطي - her negative iza-clause keeps the b-.

rows.medi_said: Is it يخربوا؟ Do I need to link it back to the روز؟
rows.amal_said: بيخرب. Yes. If you don't-- wait. No. Because the rose is in the beginning. So rose راح يخرب.
rows.why: He proposed the plural يخربوا for singular الرز; she said no, الرز راح يخرب. Offered as a question, so low.

rows.medi_said: Okay. روز راح يخرب إذا، إذا ما بتفتحي، هي الثلاجة.
rows.why: Repeating the sentence he again used فتح (open) where she had just given حط (put); she answered ممتاز. Best reading, same fix as 25:08.
rows.english: The rice will go bad if you don't put it in the fridge.

rows.why: A known, specific thing (the rice in question) needs el-; he dropped it here after saying الروز at 24:38 and 25:36. Best reading; she let it pass.

rows.amal_said: tickets.
rows.why: Listening: he did not recognise تذاكر in her example سفرتنا خربت لأنه ما في تذاكر and asked; she glossed 'tickets' (sheet: 'ticket | Tazkara | تذكرة').

rows.amal_said: عزومة is feminine or masculine؟ ... خربت.
rows.why: Subject العزومة is feminine; he said خرب, she prompted 'feminine or masculine?' and gave خربت.

rows.amal_said: ما؟ ... ما it didn't come. ... ما أجا.
rows.why: Finishing 'the gathering was ruined because ... didn't come' he stalled on the negated past; she prompted 'ما؟' and supplied ما أجا. His form is untranscribed.

rows.amal_said: Mm-mm. تنورة is skirt. ... فستانك. صح.
rows.why: For 'your dress' he said تنورة (skirt); she said mm-mm, تنورة is skirt, and he then found فستانك (sheet: 'dress | Fus6aan | فستان', 'skirt | Tannoora | تنورة').
Feminine غرفة grows -t- before the possessive ending (غرفتك); the transcript shows غرفةك and she answered mm-hmm. Best reading.
'I messed up the room by accident' - الغرف is the plural (rooms) or a clipped غرفة; she only confirmed بالغلط. Best reading; may be a dropped ة.
rows.english: I messed up the room by accident.

rows.amal_said: جلاية؟ So ... جلايتك.
rows.why: Feminine جلاية takes -t- before the possessive; he said جلايك, she prompted 'جلاية؟ So' and he fixed to جلايتك, which she confirmed.

rows.amal_said: مش، مش أزتم or it's past also.
rows.why: 'They didn't mean to' is past; he left out كان, she said 'it's past also' and he reached ما كان قصدهم (ممتاز at 42:48).

rows.medi_said: Uh, مش كان and, uh, مش...
rows.amal_said: Not مش. [تضحك] If you use can. Not can.
rows.why: ما negates verbs, مش nouns/adjectives; he said مش كان, she said 'Not مش' and he fixed to ما كان قصدهم.

rows.amal_said: So، في عندنا خلاص ما can is a verb. Because can and then the verb after it should be what؟ ... صح.
rows.why: After ما كان قصدهم the next verb is the bare present (يخربوا); he used the past kharabu, she prompted 'the verb after it should be what?' and he fixed to yecharbu.
rows.english: They didn't mean to mess up your work.

rows.amal_said: So it's بخرررب. There is a, there is a double medal here. ... No. خرب. ... When do I not put the a in command؟
rows.why: Command of the doubled-middle verb takes no a-/e- prefix; he said echarrab, she said no, خرّب, and named the rule (no 'a' with a double middle or two-consonant stems).

rows.amal_said: Did you? ... [speaks Arabic]
rows.why: 'Did you break them?' is past; he answered with present bitakhrobi, she prompted 'Did you?' and he fixed to kharabtihum, which she accepted (mm-hmm).

rows.medi_said: sawarna kharab. Uh, ... were ruined. Kharabu. No. Kha-- uh, khar- kharabu. Kharabu.
rows.amal_said: Which, which one is it? [speaks Arabic]
rows.why: Non-human plural صورنا takes the feminine singular verb; he wavered kharab / kharabu, she asked 'which one is it?' and gave the form (her Arabic untranscribed; my reading is خربت), he said 'I knew that'.

rows.medi_said: rah yitkhar-- rah titkharabi. ... Yeah, rah titkharabi. Rah atkharabt.
rows.amal_said: No two T. Why two Ts؟ شوربة is feminine. So... ... one T.
rows.why: 'You will ruin it': he used the t-prefixed get-X form (تتخرّبي, 'two Ts'); she said no two T, one T, and gave راح تخربيها.
rows.english: If you put too much salt in the soup you will ruin it.

rows.amal_said: ليش؟ You would ruin it? ... اه، راح تخربيها.
rows.why: The object 'it' (the soup) must ride on the verb; she prompted 'You would ruin it?' and he added -ha (rah titkharabiha), she confirmed راح تخربيها.

rows.amal_said: Yes, بس we're talking about شوربة. So... ... صح.
rows.why: Feminine شوربة needs تخرب; he said yikhrab, she reminded him the subject is شوربة and he fixed to tikhreb (صح).
